text: Which retina-specific genes are specific to rod photoreceptor cells (single-cell) and have no detectable mRNA in liver?
plan: Tissue category (RNA): Retina / Tissue enriched AND Cell type category (scRNA): Rod photoreceptor cells / Cell type enriched AND Tissue category (RNA): Liver / Not detected
understanding: The query asks for genes with tissue-specific RNA expression in retina, single-cell RNA specificity in rod photoreceptor cells, and absence of detectable mRNA in liver.

trail.why: "Tissue enriched" defines genes with at least four-fold higher mRNA levels in a particular tissue compared to any other tissue, matching the requirement for retina-specific genes.

The requirement asks for genes specific to rod photoreceptor cells, which matches the 'Cell type enriched' definition of having at least four-fold higher mRNA level in that cell type compared to any other cell type.
The requirement specifies no detectable mRNA in liver, which directly corresponds to the tissue 'liver' paired with the RNA category 'Not detected' (defined as mRNA below detection cut-off).
